items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (r : R), (Polynomial.taylorEquiv r).symm = Polynomial.taylorEquiv (-r)
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Polynomial Substitution Equivalence at $X + t$ is Substitution at $X - t$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] (t : R),
  (Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t).symm = Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC (-t)
items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence defined by substituting $X + t$ in polynomials is equal to the algebra equivalence defined by substituting $X - t$.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Taylor's Linear Equivalence for Degree-Less-Than Submodules
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (r : R),
  (Polynomial.taylorLinearEquiv r n).symm = Polynomial.taylorLinearEquiv (-r) n
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $ and natural number $ n $, the inverse of the Taylor linear equivalence $ 	ext{taylorLinearEquiv}(r, n) $ (which maps polynomials $ f(X) $ of degree $ <n $ to $ f(X + r) $) is equal to $ 	ext{taylorLinearEquiv}(-r, n) $, corresponding to substitution of $ X - r $. This establishes that shifting by $ -r $ reverses the $ X + r $ shift within degree-$ <n $ polynomial submodules.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Algebra Equivalence via Evaluation at $ X + C(t) $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] (t : R) (a : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.algEquivAevalXAddC t).symm a = (Polynomial.aeval (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C t)) a
items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence defined by evaluation at $ X + C(t) $ maps a polynomial $ a $ to its evaluation at $ X - C(t) $, i.e., $ (\text{algEquivAevalXAddC}_t)^{-1}(a) = \text{aeval}_{X - C(t)}(a) $.

items.informal_name: Double Composition with $-X$ Recovers Original Polynomial
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] (p : Polynomial R), (p.comp (-Polynomial.X)).comp (-Polynomial.X) = p
items.informal_description: For any commutative ring $R$ and polynomial $p \in R[X]$, composing $p$ with the polynomial $-X$ twice yields the original polynomial $p$, i.e., $(p \circ (-X)) \circ (-X) = p$.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Algebra Equivalence Induced by Negating the Indeterminate
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] (a : Polynomial R),
  Polynomial.algEquivAevalNegX.symm a = (Polynomial.aeval (-Polynomial.X)) a
items.informal_description: The inverse of the $ R $-algebra equivalence from $ R[X] $ to itself induced by substituting $ -X $ for $ X $ maps a polynomial $ a $ to the evaluation of $ a $ at $ -X $, i.e., $ \text{aeval}(-X)(a) $.

items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra isomorphism that maps polynomials via multiplication by an invertible element $ a $ and addition of $ b $ is given by evaluating at the polynomial $ \frac{1}{a}(X - b) $. Specifically, for any polynomial $ f $, applying the inverse isomorphism corresponds to substituting $ X $ with $ \frac{1}{a}(X - b) $ through the evaluation homomorphism.

  (hqp : q.comp p = Polynomial.X) (a : Polynomial R), (p.algEquivOfCompEqX q hpq hqp) a = (Polynomial.aeval p) a
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and polynomials $ p, q \in R[X] $ satisfying $ p \circ q = X $ and $ q \circ p = X $, the algebra equivalence $ \text{algEquivOfCompEqX}(p, q) $ maps any polynomial $ a \in R[X] $ to the evaluation of $ a $ at $ p $, i.e., $ \text{aeval}_p(a) $.

items.type:

  (hqp : q.comp p = Polynomial.X), (p.algEquivOfCompEqX q hpq hqp).symm = q.algEquivOfCompEqX p hqp hpq
items.informal_description: Given polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ such that $ p \circ q = X $ and $ q \circ p = X $, the inverse of the algebra equivalence $ p \circ q = X $-induced equivalence is equal to the algebra equivalence induced by swapping $ p $ and $ q $ with their composition conditions interchanged.
